summary: Org policy tag enforcement prevents cross-project service-role assumption for staging->prod bridge
description:
Issue Summary:
The new organization policy enforcing resource tags (tag:team & tag:env) on service account creation is blocking the automated cross-project service-role assumption used by the staging->prod debug bridge. This prevents oncall and SRE playbooks that create short-lived service roles in staging and assume them from prod for debugging data-plane issues.

Impact:
- Immediate: Cannot complete planned production-safe debug sessions that require assuming a staging-scoped service role from prod (affects SRE oncall playbooks).
- Scope: Intermittent and reproducible for any automatic provisioning flow that creates service accounts without the new org tags. Affects both GCP and AWS bridging flows when orchestration creates corresponding cloud roles.

Root Cause Hypothesis:
- Org policy (tag-guard) rolled out 2026-02-27 requires tag:team and tag:env on service account/role create. Automated bridge tooling (priv-bridge) creates service accounts via a legacy service principal that does not include tags in the create call, so creation appears to succeed but the resource is non-compliant and cannot be assumed across projects due to deny policies on assume-role/impersonation.

Observed Behavior (examples):
- gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy staging-sa@staging-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com returns policy but Cloud Audit shows a DENY entry tied to org policy enforcement.
- aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/staging-bridge-role returns AccessDenied with context "TagComplianceFailure" in CloudTrail.

Expected Behavior:
- Automated bridge tooling should create tagged service accounts/roles (tag:team=platform, tag:env=staging) so cross-project assume/impersonate flows succeed and audit logs show compliant resources.

Temporary Workaround:
- Manual creation of a tagged service account/role in staging by a user with OrgPolicy bypass privileges (security-admin) allows assume to succeed. Not scalable and requires elevated privileges.

Proposed Fix:
1) Update priv-bridge provisioning code to include required org tags at creation time for both GCP and AWS resources.
2) Add a preflight check in the onboarding flow that validates org policy constraints and fails early with actionable message.
3) Run a backfill job to detect non-compliant service accounts created between 2026-02-27 and 2026-03-01 and fix tags or recreate them.
steps_to_reproduce: From prod project with normal SRE permissions, trigger priv-bridge to create a staging-scoped service account (use the existing pipeline).
Observe provisioning logs (priv-bridge) that show createServiceAccount succeeded with HTTP 200 but audit log contains ORG_POLICY_DENY for tag requirements.
Attempt to assume/impersonate the newly created account from prod: run gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=... and then gcloud auth print-access-token or aws sts assume-role equivalent.
Observe AccessDenied and trace id in Cloud Audit/CloudTrail referencing TagComplianceFailure or org policy deny.

2026-03-01T09:12:46Z prod: attempt impersonate -> ERROR: Permission denied: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken - context=TagComplianceFailure
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Confirmed timing of org policy rollout (2026-02-27). Policy requires keys tag:team and tag:env for service account/role creation across org. Policy scope: staging and prod folders.

2026-03-02 Ravi Patel: Reproduced locally with a minimal create call: gcloud iam service-accounts create test-sa --project=staging-project (no tags passed) results in audit DENY. Passing tags via API (projects.serviceAccounts.create with iam.serviceAccounts.createRequest.resourceMetadata) succeeds.
2026-03-03 Security: Raised that there's no automated alert for non-compliant SA creation; suggested a Config Rule to detect non-compliant resources in next 48h.
2026-03-04 Infra: Priv-bridge code path uses googleapiclient v1 wrapper that did not expose resource metadata fields for tags; patch required in internal library.

2026-03-04 Ops: Backfill plan sketched: list all SAs created since 2026-02-27 with missing tags, attempt to patch add tags where supported, otherwise create replacement with proper tag set and rotate keys.
comments: 2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Filing ticket after reproducing failure in staging. Marking P1 because it blocks oncall debug flows.
2026-03-02 Ravi Patel: Assigned to me. I can push a small change to priv-bridge to include tags in create calls; need a library bump and a short canary in staging.
2026-03-03 Security (A. Gomez): We cannot grant orgpolicy bypass broadly; prefer code fix + backfill. Will help with runbooks for manual escalation if needed.
2026-03-04 Infra (L. Novak): Found where the library strips metadata. Preparing a patch and will open a PR this afternoon.
2026-03-05 Ravi Patel: PR opened (see related_github_prs). Holding for review; created a short rollback plan and a staged backfill job plan.
next_steps: Merge priv-bridge library patch that surfaces resource metadata for tags (owner: Ravi Patel).
Deploy canary to staging and validate that newly created SAs include tag:team=platform and tag:env=staging and can be assumed from prod.
Run backfill job to fix non-compliant SAs created 2026-02-27..2026-03-01; prepare rotation plan for keys if replacement occurs (owner: Infrastructure).
Add detection rule to org-config that alerts when non-compliant SAs are created (owner: Security).
